boards.title: Your First Weekend at Ithaca College, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A Friday-to-Sunday sequence for learning the South Hill campus, sharing meals, finding recreation, exploring the arts and trails, and meeting downtown Ithaca.

cards.title: Start at the Information Desk
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Campus Center main lobby
cards.notes: Ask the student staff for directions, current service hours, and one campus event that fits your first-weekend schedule.
cards.short_summary: Use the staffed desk to turn arrival questions into a workable weekend plan.
cards.evidence_claim: The Campus Center Information Desk is in the main lobby, where student staff provide directions, service hours, and information about Ithaca-area attractions.
cards.access_notes: The Campus Center lists 2026 summer building hours of 7:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m. daily and desk staffing from 9:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m.; semester hours may differ.

cards.title: Share the First Dinner
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · Campus Center Dining Hall
cards.notes: Check the weekly menu together, identify dietary stations before joining a line, and use the meal to compare weekend plans.
cards.short_summary: Begin the social part of the weekend around a flexible campus meal.
cards.evidence_claim: Campus Center Dining Hall serves breakfast, lunch, and dinner offerings, including deli, grain, pizza, gluten-free, kosher, and vegan options.
cards.access_notes: Dining schedules change by term; consult the linked dining page and current Locations & Hours listing before going.

cards.title: Make Friday a Game Night
cards.subtitle: Friday night · First floor of Phillips Hall
cards.notes: Bring your IC ID, choose a quick round of Ping-Pong, foosball, billiards, or a board game, and invite someone new to join.
cards.short_summary: A low-pressure game gives the group something to do while introductions settle in.
cards.evidence_claim: The Campus Center Recreation Center offers Ping-Pong, billiards, foosball, and board games to people with a valid Ithaca College ID.
cards.access_notes: The current page lists Friday hours of noon–midnight and Saturday hours of 5:00 p.m.–midnight; valid Ithaca College ID required.

cards.title: Open Saturday with Art
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · Gannett Center ground floor
cards.notes: Confirm that an exhibition is installed, then pick one work to photograph if permitted and discuss outside the gallery afterward.
cards.short_summary: A compact gallery visit creates an easy first shared conversation about campus art.
cards.evidence_claim: Handwerker Gallery is an Ithaca College exhibition space in the Gannett Center and lists Saturday gallery hours of 10:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Saturday hours are listed as 10:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m. The gallery closes between exhibitions, so verify the exhibition calendar first.

cards.title: Move Before Lunch
cards.subtitle: Saturday midday · Campus Center Quad
cards.notes: Bring your IC ID and clean sneakers, start with a short familiar workout, and ask the desk before borrowing recreation equipment.
cards.short_summary: Use a brief workout to learn where campus recreation fits into an ordinary week.
cards.evidence_claim: Ithaca College students can use their ID for free access to Fitness Center equipment and facilities, with free equipment rentals available to valid-ID campus members.
cards.access_notes: Fall 2026 hours begin August 24; the page lists Saturday 11:00 a.m.–7:00 p.m. Access requires a valid Ithaca College ID.

cards.title: Try the Other Dining Hall
cards.subtitle: Saturday lunch · Terrace 1 ground floor
cards.notes: Compare the posted menu with Friday’s meal, locate the Minus 3 and Kosher options, and choose a meeting point before separating.
cards.short_summary: A second dining hall helps new students learn another practical campus routine.
cards.evidence_claim: Terrace Dining Hall is on the ground floor of Terrace 1 and provides breakfast, lunch, and dinner service with gluten-free, kosher, and vegan options.
cards.access_notes: The dining page says to use a meal swipe and provides a weekly-menu link; verify term-specific operating hours before visiting.

cards.title: Walk the Natural Lands
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Campus trail system
cards.notes: Open the trail information before leaving, choose a route that matches the group’s mobility and daylight, and stay on marked paths.
cards.short_summary: A daylight walk introduces the protected forest surrounding the South Hill campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Ithaca College Natural Lands encompasses more than 560 protected acres and offers more than seven miles of trails for education, research, and recreation.
cards.access_notes: Use trails only in daylight, check current trail information and weather, stay on marked routes, and select terrain appropriate for the group.

cards.entity_name: Ithaca College Athletics and Events Center
cards.title: Catch a Home Competition
cards.subtitle: Saturday evening · Athletics and Events Center
cards.notes: Check the official Bombers schedule for a home contest, confirm its venue and start time, and arrive early enough to find seating.
cards.short_summary: A scheduled home event offers a clear, school-centered way to spend Saturday evening.
cards.evidence_claim: Ithaca College states that admission to all home athletic events is free and identifies the Athletics and Events Center as a major competition facility.
cards.access_notes: A game is not guaranteed every weekend; consult the official Bombers schedule and confirm the listed venue, time, and entry details.

cards.title: Take a Quiet Sunday Pause
cards.subtitle: Sunday morning · Muller Chapel
cards.notes: Use the gathering space for quiet reflection or study, keep voices low, and check the events calendar before entering a program.
cards.short_summary: The chapel supplies an inclusive, calm reset before the weekend’s final outing.
cards.evidence_claim: Muller Chapel is open every day for quiet meditation and study and supports religious, spiritual, and mindfulness programming.
cards.access_notes: The chapel is listed as open daily from 8:00 a.m.–10:00 p.m.; an accessible entrance is on the north side near the pond.

cards.title: Finish Downtown on Foot
cards.subtitle: Sunday afternoon · Downtown Ithaca pedestrian zone
cards.notes: Walk the four-block pedestrian area, choose its performance space as the group’s regrouping point, and keep purchases optional.
cards.short_summary: The final stop connects the South Hill campus weekend with Ithaca’s downtown public space.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Ithaca identifies Ithaca Commons as a four-block pedestrian-only downtown zone with seating, shops, eateries, and a performance space.
cards.access_notes: This is a public pedestrian zone; check city notices and transit schedules before traveling from campus, and arrange the return trip in advance.
